label: Breadcrumbs
title: Breadcrumbs
summary: Use Breadcrumbs when people need a compact path back through a hierarchy. The trail moves from the broadest ancestor to the current page.
corePrinciple: Preserve route order and keep the current page visible. Chevrons, link treatment, and current-page state are supplied by the published component.

anatomy.title: A path with a clear endpoint
anatomy.description: Read the route from ancestor to current and keep the component secondary to the page heading.
blocks: The published component communicates hierarchy without replacing the page title or primary navigation.
Items are ordered from the broadest ancestor toward the current page. Each ancestor can take people back one level.
Separators express the path between items. Do not add manual punctuation or duplicate chevrons.
The last item is current unless an explicit current item is supplied. The published story identifies the current page.

configuration.title: Configuration follows the route
configuration.description: Breadcrumbs has no exposed properties in the inspected Figma source. Configure content hierarchy and let the published component render the path.
blocks: Order each item from the broadest ancestor to the current page.
A constrained parent lets a long trail wrap. The component does not auto-collapse the route.
Select an ancestor to preview navigation.
The final item reads as current unless the published component receives an explicit current item.

states.title: States follow hierarchy and width
states.description: The published stories show a default trail, a long trail, and interactive ancestors. Width and route data drive the outcome.
blocks: Items wrap within the constrained parent.
Select an ancestor to preview navigation.
Ancestor items can navigate; current remains current.
The trail reflects hierarchy and available width. Do not represent a responsive collapse or item count as a designer-selected control.

sizing.title: The parent supplies the constraint
sizing.description: A Breadcrumbs trail stays in the available parent and wraps when the route is longer than the line.
blocks: Width comes from the parent. A long trail wraps inside the available space; it does not auto-collapse into a menu.

content.title: Make the relationship visible
content.description: Breadcrumbs works when the route has meaningful ancestors and the current page needs orientation.
blocks: Order items from the broadest ancestor toward the current page.
Keep the final item concise and aligned with the page title.
A constrained parent can wrap a long path; it does not invent a different navigation pattern.
Breadcrumbs supports orientation. It should not compete with primary navigation or the page heading.

inContext.title: Place the primitive where the relationship happens
inContext.description: Use Breadcrumbs above page content when the route supports backtracking.
blocks: Orient people above a report page when the route has meaningful ancestors.
Keep a long route in its constrained parent so people can still parse each level.
The current page should agree with the visible heading and carry current-page semantics.
Select an ancestor to preview navigation.

doDont.title: Protect structure and clarity
doDont.description: These pairs keep hierarchy readable and leave route behavior to the published component.
blocks: Order the trail from ancestor to current
The route becomes easier to scan and the current page has a clear endpoint.
Reverse the route to match a visual shortcut
The reading order stops matching the hierarchy and current location becomes ambiguous.
Let a long trail wrap inside its parent
Available width stays visible and the route remains available for orientation.
The component does not decide to replace route levels with an ellipsis menu.
